title: US Parents Say Having a Baby Is Too Expensive
paragraphs: Having a baby is one of the biggest moments in many people's lives. But according to a new poll, most parents in the US feel that it has become far too expensive.

The poll was carried out by the University of Michigan Health C.S. Mott Children's Hospital as part of its National Poll on Children's Health. In July, it asked 2,027 parents across the US about the costs of having and raising young children. The results were published in October 2026.

The poll found that four out of five parents, or 81%, believe that having a baby costs more than it should. In addition, two in five parents of children aged three and under described their financial situation as "struggling" or "just getting by." More than a third of these parents said they worry about money all the time.

Parents mentioned many necessary and important costs, including diapers, car seats, healthy food and good childcare. To deal with these costs, many families are finding ways to save money. About 68% of parents with young children said they used secondhand baby clothes and equipment. Many also said they had cut back on extras, saved money in advance or worked extra hours.

Many parents would also like more help from the government. About three in five said they support government programs to reduce financial pressure on families. The most popular idea was paid leave from work during pregnancy or after a baby is born.

Sarah Clark, the co-director of the poll, said that items like diapers, safe car seats, healthy food and quality childcare are important for a child's health, safety and development. Clark added that these are not simply optional purchases or extras in a family's budget.
